summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, cardiomyopathy due to Chagas disease, and a history of coronary artery bypass grafting presented during a dialysis session with hypotension and bradycardia. He was found to have severe hyperkalemia with a potassium level of 8.6, leading to an idioventricular rhythm. He was treated in the emergency department with calcium gluconate, insulin, dextrose, and atropine, and underwent emergent hemodialysis, which normalized his potassium. His bradycardia and hypotension resolved, and he was weaned off dopamine. His home lisinopril dose was reduced to 20 mg daily to minimize potassium elevation risk. He reported mild diarrhea and possible missed medications prior to admission. Blood cultures showed no growth, and chest imaging revealed stable pleural effusions without signs of infection. He recovered well, restarted his insulin regimen, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete all dialysis sessions and monitor weight.
